title: Tommy Dorsey hires him after the Dartmouth Battle of Music
summary: Dorsey, needing a drummer after Dave Tough, hires him because Shaw's band beat Dorsey's at the Dartmouth Winter Carnival; Leeman starts June 19, 1939.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Right, and they were playing the old Orchard Beach, another one of those places. Another one of my expeditions there. So I was very unhappy about making a comeback after being ill, and I went home, and about two or three days later, I got a call from Tommy Dorsey's manager, who was with a real great band at that time at the old Pennsylvania Hotel Roof Garden.
Well, what year was this, Cliff?
1939. This is a few weeks after I was discouraged because Glenn Miller wasn't bringing me back. Well, Tommy had had trouble with Dave Tough who was on one of his famous toots.

Yes, a great drummer. And Tommy needed a new drummer, so they called me and wanted to know if I'd like to come and try out. But Tommy knew me from having a Battle of Music, and the Battle of Music at Dartmouth College,
and it's an old stroy now that only some of the old timers can tell, because he was the name band, he was the biggest band playing at the Dartmouth Winter Carnival in the gymnasium.
What year was this now? Do you remember?
Now you're up to 1939 now, remember?
Well, we just got through joining Tommy Dorsey in 1939.

No, no. Tommy knew me from a Battle of Music with Artie Shaw when we cut them -- Billie Holiday was singing with us, and we cut his great band which was the number one band at Dartmouth College Winter Carnival. He knew my reputation as a drummer because we cut them a brand new one -- that's how that goes, so that's why he wanted me to come with his orchestra. That's what little reputation I had spread around with Artie Shaw, and so I went down, and was accepted by Tommy Dorsey. I arrived June 19th, 1939. I went to work that day, and because I had been ill in Portland, Maine, the past few months -- they granted me my card outright. The New York local. Or I couldn't have worked with the band. And that's why it's like indelible ink on my mind.
